subject.title: RFC: Readiness Conditions and Standard Hosting Profiles

question: Should OpenClaw evolve its established Gateway-owned readiness model into the proposed canonical condition, plugin-provider, and standard-profile contracts, and should those public surfaces be accepted together or staged after core-condition normalization?
rationale: Current main does not already provide these capabilities, and the choice creates durable API, configuration, upgrade, readiness-policy, and release-support commitments that automated review cannot authorize.

options.title: Stage core conditions first
options.body: Accept normalization of existing readiness and legacy projections first, then review plugin providers, operator profiles, and non-local profile promises as proof-gated follow-ups.

options.title: Accept the combined contract
options.body: Approve the complete condition, provider, profile, configuration-precedence, and release-conformance direction with explicit compatibility ownership.

options.title: Retain current boundaries
options.body: Keep readiness Gateway-owned and leave hosting-specific or plugin-specific composition to downstream checks and existing extension surfaces.

recommendation.title: Stage core conditions first
recommendation.body: Accept normalization of existing readiness and legacy projections first, then review plugin providers, operator profiles, and non-local profile promises as proof-gated follow-ups.

likelyOwner.reason: The sampled history shows the strongest combined involvement in current Gateway readiness, plugin registries, and repository-level integration decisions.
